---
title: "Avocado Oil Authenticity"
format: html
---

## Question

How often were processed foods made with avocado oil authentic, compared with foods made with olive oil?

## Data

The data come from the [TidyTuesday project](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2026/2026-10-06) and were curated from a 2026 UC Davis study.
Researchers tested two lots of chips, mayonnaise, and salad dressing products to see whether their chemical profiles were consistent with the oil named on the package.

```{r}
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)

oil_foods <- read_csv(
  "avocado_oil_processed_foods.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

## Visualization

```{r}
authenticity <- oil_foods |>
  group_by(oil_type, category) |>
  summarize(
    products_tested = n(),
    authentic_percent = mean(authentic) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    category = str_to_title(str_replace_all(category, "_", " ")),
    oil_type = str_to_title(oil_type)
  )

ggplot(
  authenticity,
  aes(x = category, y = authentic_percent, fill = oil_type)
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = str_c(round(authentic_percent), "%")),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
    vjust = -0.3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Avocado" = "#6B8E23", "Olive" = "#D4A017")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 110)) +
  labs(
    title = "Avocado oil claims rarely passed authenticity testing",
    subtitle = "Olive oil products passed nearly every test across all three categories",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Authentic samples (%)",
    fill = "Oil on label",
    caption = "TidyTuesday 2026-10-06 | Source: UC Davis"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

Only 7% of avocado-oil chip samples and 29% of avocado-oil mayonnaise samples were authentic, while none of the avocado-oil salad dressings passed.
In comparison, 90% to 100% of the olive-oil samples were authentic in each category.
The dataset contains only 74 lot-level samples, so the results describe the products tested rather than every product on the market.
